auto.features.tutorial.lib.steps.literal: Three steps: pick a file and mark one or more input columns (text from several columns is combined in each row), choose a labelling mode, then define a question or categories. After that you move on to the labelling itself, with keyboard navigation and export at the end.

Beyond the browser interface, the optimised prompt is immediately available through a REST API. Copy the endpoint URL or use the ready-made code snippets (Python, JavaScript, cURL) to integrate it into your own code.

Free-text search across all runs in the system — yours or other users'. Type a description in English or Hebrew, and Skynet finds runs with similar meaning, not just word matches. When the field is empty it suggests your recent searches and common searches, and you can focus the field from anywhere with the keyboard. You can filter by models, optimisers, status, and date range, and browse a ranked list of results.
Four cards summarise activity: all runs, active runs, succeeded runs, and failed runs, alongside success and failure rates.
auto.features.tutorial.lib.steps.templat: {p1} produces the answers. {p2} analyses errors and proposes prompt improvements. You can choose a different {p3} for each role.

At the top there is navigation to the dashboard, text labelling, submitting a new {p1}, and semantic search across existing runs. At the bottom, the run history appears grouped by date. Through the ⋯ next to a {p2} you can share, rename, clone, pin, or delete.
Each example from the {p1} is shown with a colour-coded {p2} (green = high, red = low), the {p3} prediction, and the split into {p4}, {p5}, and {p6}. You can sort by {p7} to spot patterns.
After the run finishes, you can test the optimised prompt in real time. Enter a new input and get an immediate prediction from the {p1}.
A tool for labelling {p1}s directly in the system. Upload a CSV, JSON, or Excel file, choose a labelling mode, and label row by row. When you're done you can export the results.
Now you know Skynet's main capabilities. Submit your first {p1}, follow the {p2} in real time, and test the optimised prompt in the Usage tab.
A performance chart that shows, for each run, the {p1} as normalised quality, alongside relative speed when time data is available. Below it, a table comparing {p2} against the {p3} for each run.
